title: Is the mean-field's overshoot on the ring crowd caused by finite-size noise or by memory correlation?
lede: A noisy memoryless map tips at 0.06 robot share for spread robots, the simulation at 0.10 and the mean-field at 0.18 (k = 2), but an audit found the gap is mostly a horizon mismatch and a mean-field rounding artefact, not memory.
summary: Three models of the ring walking-side game (N = 200, M = 9, ε = 0.02, 20 seeds) are compared on the smallest robot share that tips the crowd: the deterministic mean-field of society-ringmf, a noisy memoryless resampling variant, and the society-allies simulation. The simulation lies between the other two in 6 of 6 cells (spread robots at k = 2: 0.06 / 0.10 / 0.18), but a 2026-11-19 audit found the bracketing disappears when the resampled model is run for the simulation's memory turnover (56 sweeps, not 300) or the mean-field uses the exact binomial, so it does not separate noise from memory. Limits: only 6 cells; the resampling model also changes update order, which is not separated from memory; thresholds ±0.02; M and ε are not sourced; 1D binary game.
